scene.speaker: ingrid
scene.bubble: Every great expedition learns from the past. Today: real explorers who crossed oceans, jungles and ice!
scene.intro: Every great expedition learns from the past. Maya tells the class about explorers who crossed oceans in wooden ships, who drew the first maps of coasts nobody had seen, and who climbed mountains without modern equipment. Some discovered new places; many simply came home and wrote everything down. Ingrid takes notes. Which explorer would YOU like to be? Tell their story in the past!

activities.title: Quick check · Read about Roald Amundsen and choose the right answer.

data.instructions: Read the text. Choose the correct answer.
data.text: Roald Amundsen was born in Norway in 1872. As a boy, he slept with his window open in winter to prepare his body for the cold! In 1911 he led the first team that reached the South Pole. They travelled with four sledges and fifty-two dogs, and they planted the Norwegian flag on the ice on the 14th of December. Amundsen wrote in his diary that the journey was hard, but his team was strong and well prepared. Today, a sea near Antarctica has his name.

activities.title: Listen to Maya's explorer facts. Write a word or number in each gap.

data.script: Maya: Explorer facts, Ingrid! Fact one: the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic was Amelia Earhart, in 1932. … Ingrid: Alone, over all that ocean. So brave! … Maya: Fact two: María Reiche studied the Nazca lines in Peru for fifty years! … Maya: She cleaned the desert lines with her own broom. … Ingrid: A broom! That's dedication. … Maya: Fact three: the first team on top of Everest carried oxygen in heavy metal bottles. … Maya: And fact four: today explorers use satellites, but they still carry paper maps. Just in case! … Ingrid: Rule number one of every expedition: always have a plan B.

activities.title: Grammar · Before she sailed, after she returned
activities.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose the right word.
activities.structure: Before / after clauses (not with future reference)

data.title: Before she sailed, after she returned
data.intro: Before and after put two past actions in order. Careful: the order of the words is not always the order of the story.
data.can: I can put two past actions in order with before and after.

examples.text: I finished my homework before I played football.
Before she sailed to the pole, Ingrid studied the map for a year.
After they climbed the mountain, they wrote everything down.
The explorers ate their breakfast before they left the ship.

rules: before / after + a whole clause: a person and a verb, not just a word.
Both verbs are in the past simple: before she sailed, after they climbed.
Read to the end before you decide what happened first — that is exactly what the exam asks you to do.

items.sentence: First they climbed the mountain. Then they took a photo. So they took a photo ___ they climbed it.
___ they left the ship, the explorers looked at the map one last time.
After she ___ home, she wrote a book about her journey.
He read the map carefully before he ___ the ship.

options: Before the journey started, they got everything ready.
Before started the journey, they got everything ready.
Before, the journey started they got everything ready.
